subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: Which boundary commission was appointed under the chairmanship of Sir Cyril Radcliffe to demarcate the borders between India and Pakistan in 1947?
questions.explanation: Sir Cyril Radcliffe chaired the two boundary commissions appointed in 1947 to demarcate the borders dividing Punjab and Bengal between India and Pakistan.

questions.question: Who served as the first Chief Election Commissioner of independent India during the historic first General Elections of 1951-52?
questions.explanation: Sukumar Sen was appointed as India's first Chief Election Commissioner in 1950 and successfully conducted the first general elections in 1951-52.

questions.sub_topic: Planning Commission and Five Year Plans
questions.question: In which year was the Planning Commission of India established by an executive resolution of the Government of India?
questions.explanation: The Planning Commission was set up in March 1950 by an executive resolution of the Union Government, with Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru as its first Chairman.

questions.question: The historic Afro-Asian Conference of 1955 that served as the precursor to the Non-Aligned Movement was held in which city?
questions.explanation: The Bandung Conference was held in Bandung, Indonesia, in April 1955, establishing the groundwork for Afro-Asian solidarity and the Non-Aligned Movement.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: The non-Congress coalition governments formed in several Indian states following the 1967 general elections were commonly termed as:
questions.explanation: Following the 1967 general elections, non-Congress legislative coalitions formed joint governments in various northern states known as Samyukta Vidhayak Dal (SVD) governments.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution was the National Emergency declared on 25 June 1975 on grounds of internal disturbance?
questions.explanation: The National Emergency proclaimed by President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed on 25 June 1975 was invoked under Article 352 of the Indian Constitution citing internal disturbance.

questions.question: The military operation conducted in June 1984 to flush out militants from the Golden Temple complex in Amritsar was code-named:
questions.explanation: Operation Blue Star was the code name given to the Indian military action carried out in June 1984 to clear armed militants from the Golden Temple in Amritsar.

questions.question: The Chipko Movement originated in the early 1970s in which present-day Indian state?
questions.explanation: The Chipko movement began in 1973 in the Chamoli district of the Garhwal region, which was then part of Uttar Pradesh and is now located in Uttarakhand.

questions.question: The Second Backward Classes Commission appointed by the Janata Party government in 1979 was chaired by:
questions.explanation: Bindeshwari Prasad Mandal (B.P. Mandal) headed the Second Backward Classes Commission, officially appointed in January 1979 to investigate conditions of socially and educationally backward classes.

questions.question: NITI Aayog, which replaced the Planning Commission of India in January 2015, stands for:
options: A) National Institute of Technology and Innovation
B) National Institution for Transforming India
C) National Initiative for Technical Integration
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog stands for the National Institution for Transforming India, established on 1 January 2015 as the think-tank of the Union Government.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: Which military alliance was founded by the Soviet Union and its Eastern European allies in 1955 to counter NATO?
questions.explanation: The Warsaw Pact (Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance) was formed in May 1955 by the Soviet Union and Eastern bloc countries as a counterweight to NATO.

questions.question: In which month and year was the Berlin Wall brought down by the citizens of East and West Germany, symbolizing the end of the Cold War divide in Europe?
questions.explanation: The Berlin Wall was demolished by ordinary German citizens on 9 November 1989, unifying the city and marking the beginning of the collapse of the Eastern communist bloc.

questions.question: The UN-mandated international military coalition operation that liberated Kuwait from Iraqi occupation in 1991 was known as:
questions.explanation: Operation Desert Storm was the code name for the 1991 US-led coalition military assault that liberated Kuwait after Saddam Hussein's invasion.

questions.question: The common currency introduced by members of the European Union in 1999 for non-physical transactions and in 2002 as physical cash is the:
questions.explanation: The Euro was launched as the official single currency of the European Union, adopted in 1999 for accountancy and circulating as banknotes and coins from 1 January 2002.

questions.question: Which founding document signed in August 1967 brought the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) into existence?
questions.explanation: The ASEAN Bangkok Declaration was signed on 8 August 1967 by the foreign ministers of Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand.

questions.question: In which South Asian capital city was the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) founded in December 1985?
questions.explanation: The SAARC charter was formally adopted and signed by the heads of state of South Asian countries in Dhaka, Bangladesh, on 8 December 1985.

questions.question: How many permanent members hold the veto power in the United Nations Security Council?
questions.explanation: The United Nations Security Council has five permanent members (P5: United States, United Kingdom, France, Russia, and China) who possess veto rights.

questions.question: The international convention prohibiting the development, production, and stockpiling of bacteriological weapons, opened for signature in 1972, is commonly called:
questions.explanation: The Biological Weapons Convention (BWC) of 1972 banned the development, production, stockpiling, and acquisition of biological and toxin weapons.

questions.question: The United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED), also popularly known as the Earth Summit, was held in 1992 in:
questions.explanation: The Earth Summit took place in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, in June 1992, producing Agenda 21, the Rio Declaration, and frameworks on climate and biodiversity.

questions.question: The global civil society coalition that meets to oppose neo-liberal globalisation and advocate alternatives under the slogan 'Another World is Possible' is the:
questions.explanation: The World Social Forum (WSF) was established in 2001 in Porto Alegre, Brazil, uniting activists, NGOs, and trade unions against corporate-led neo-liberal globalisation.

questions.question: Which political philosophy was formulated by Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyaya as the official ideological bedrock of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh?
questions.explanation: Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyaya presented the doctrine of Integral Humanism in 1965, placing the holistic well-being of the human being at the center of social and economic organization.

questions.question: The ruler of which princely state signed the Instrument of Accession with the Government of India in September 1948 only after the military action known as 'Operation Polo'?
questions.explanation: The Nizam of Hyderabad resisted accession and deployed the communal militia Razakars, leading the Indian government to launch Operation Polo in September 1948 to secure integration.

questions.question: The Second Five Year Plan (1956-1961) placed principal emphasis on heavy industrialisation and import substitution under the leadership of which renowned statistician?
questions.explanation: The Second Five Year Plan, widely known as the Nehru-Mahalanobis Plan, was drafted under the guidance of Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis and championed rapid heavy industrialisation.

questions.question: The Tashkent Agreement signed in January 1966 to formalize peace following the 1965 Indo-Pak war was mediated by which world power?
questions.explanation: Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin mediated the Tashkent negotiations in Uzbekistan (USSR) between Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri and Pakistani President Ayub Khan.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: During the 1969 presidential election, who was the official nominee of the Congress Syndicate defeated by the independent candidate V.V. Giri supported by Indira Gandhi?
questions.explanation: The official candidate selected by the Congress Parliamentary Board (dominated by the Syndicate) was Neelam Sanjiva Reddy, who was defeated by V.V. Giri after Indira Gandhi appealed for a conscience vote.

questions.question: Who led the nationwide Railway Strike of May 1974 demanding bonus and improved service conditions, which was forcefully suppressed by the Union Government?
questions.explanation: George Fernandes, as President of the All India Railwaymen's Federation, led the historic 20-day nationwide railway strike in May 1974.

questions.question: The commission of inquiry appointed by the Janata Party government in May 1977 to investigate excesses, abuses of authority, and malpractices committed during the Emergency was headed by:
questions.explanation: The Union government established the Shah Commission under retired Supreme Court Chief Justice J.C. Shah to investigate excesses committed during the Emergency.

questions.question: The 1986 peace agreement between the Government of India and the Mizo National Front, terminating two decades of insurgency, was signed by Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and which insurgent leader?
questions.explanation: The Mizo Peace Accord was concluded in June 1986 between Rajiv Gandhi's administration and MNF chief Laldenga, making Mizoram a full-fledged state with Laldenga as Chief Minister.

questions.question: In January 1988, thousands of farmers staged a massive multi-week sit-in outside the Commissioner's office in Meerut under the banner of the Bharatiya Kisan Union led by:
questions.explanation: Mahendra Singh Tikait headed the Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU) during the iconic 1988 Meerut demonstration demanding higher sugarcane prices and cancellation of electricity rate hikes.

questions.question: The National Front government formed in December 1989 under Prime Minister V.P. Singh was supported from the outside by which unusual combination of political forces?
options: A) Indian National Congress and AIADMK
B) Bharatiya Janata Party and the Left Front
C) Samajwadi Party and Bahujan Samaj Party
D) Shiv Sena and Akali Dal exclusively
questions.explanation: V.P. Singh's National Front minority government was sustained from the outside simultaneously by two ideological adversaries: the Right-wing BJP and the Left Front.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: The installation of nuclear missiles in Cuba by Soviet Premier Nikita Khrushchev in October 1962 triggered a tense standoff with which United States President?
questions.explanation: US President John F. Kennedy blockaded naval routes around Cuba in October 1962 after US spy planes photographed Soviet nuclear missile launch sites installed by Khrushchev.

questions.question: Who was elected as the first President of the Russian Federation in 1991 and played a pivotal role in dismantling the Soviet Union?
questions.explanation: Boris Yeltsin emerged as the popular Russian leader resisting the hardline August 1991 coup and declared the dissolution of the USSR alongside the leaders of Ukraine and Belarus in December 1991.

questions.question: The abrupt transition from an authoritarian socialist economy to a free-market capitalist system in the post-Soviet republics, guided by the IMF and World Bank, was known as:
questions.explanation: Shock Therapy was the abrupt transition model imposed in Russia and Eastern Europe that involved immediate price liberalisation, privatization vouchers, and trade deregulations.

questions.question: In response to the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001, the United States launched which military campaign targeting the Taliban and Al-Qaeda in Afghanistan?
questions.explanation: Operation Enduring Freedom was launched in October 2001 by US President George W. Bush as part of the Global War on Terror against the Taliban regime and Al-Qaeda in Afghanistan.

questions.question: Which treaty signed in February 1992 formally established the European Union and paved the way for common foreign policy and monetary union?
questions.explanation: The Maastricht Treaty (Treaty on European Union) was signed on 7 February 1992 by members of the European Community, entering into force on 1 November 1993.

questions.question: The 'Open Door Policy' and modern economic reforms in the People's Republic of China were officially announced in December 1978 by which Chinese leader?
questions.explanation: Deng Xiaoping unveiled the Open Door policy and the Four Modernisations in December 1978, shifting China toward a socialist market economy and attracting foreign investment.

questions.sub_topic: Indo-Pak Treaties and River Water Sharing
questions.question: The Indus Waters Treaty of September 1960, allocating the waters of the Indus river basin between India and Pakistan, was negotiated with the mediation of:
options: B) The International Court of Justice
C) The United Nations General Assembly
questions.explanation: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in Karachi in September 1960 by Prime Minister Nehru and President Ayub Khan after successful mediation by the World Bank (then IBRD).

questions.question: Which international organisation was created in 1957 following US President Dwight Eisenhower's 'Atoms for Peace' proposal to promote the peaceful use of nuclear technology?
questions.explanation: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) was established in 1957 as an autonomous organization to promote the peaceful use of nuclear energy and prevent its diversion to military purposes.

questions.question: The seminal 1987 report of the World Commission on Environment and Development that popularized the definition of 'sustainable development' was titled:
questions.explanation: The Brundtland Commission (chaired by Gro Harlem Brundtland) published 'Our Common Future' in 1987, defining sustainable development as meeting present needs without compromising future generations.

questions.question: In the debate over cultural globalisation, the emergence of a uniform global culture dominated by Western consumerism is referred to as:
questions.explanation: Cultural homogenisation refers to the spread of a standardized, singular culture across the globe, frequently characterized by Western habits, clothing, and commercial practices.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the States Reorganisation Commission (SRC) appointed in 1953:
1. It was chaired by Justice Fazal Ali, with K.M. Panikkar and H.N. Kunzru as members.
2. The Commission completely rejected language as a basis for internal administrative borders.
3. Based on its recommendations, the States Reorganisation Act 1956 created 14 states and 6 Union Territories.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Commission accepted linguistic uniformity as a primary criterion for reorganising state boundaries, while balancing security and economic considerations.

questions.question:
Match the economic thinkers and leaders with their prominent contributions or associations during early Indian planning:
(a) J.C. Kumarappa — 1. Chief architect of the Second Five Year Plan
(b) P.C. Mahalanobis — 2. Resigned over agricultural neglect and founded Bharatiya Kranti Dal
(c) K.N. Raj — 3. Authored 'Economy of Permanence' advocating rural industrialisation
(d) Chaudhary Charan Singh — 4. Young economist associated with drafting the First Five Year Plan
Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: J.C. Kumarappa authored 'Economy of Permanence' emphasizing Gandhian village industries. P.C. Mahalanobis framed the Second Plan for heavy industry. K.N. Raj was a key young economist drafting the First Plan. Charan Singh split from Congress over the neglect of agriculture to champion farmer interests.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT among the five principles of peaceful coexistence (Panchsheel) signed between Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Premier Zhou Enlai on 29 April 1954?
options: A) Mutual respect for each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty
B) Mutual non-aggression and mutual non-interference in internal affairs
C) Mutual agreement to form joint defense military pacts against foreign aggression
D) Equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence
questions.explanation: Panchsheel strictly committed both nations to non-alignment and non-interference, completely eschewing military alliances, joint pacts, or mutual defense commitments.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Which constitutional amendment bill was brought by Indira Gandhi's government in 1971 to abolish the Privy Purses and privileges previously granted to former rulers of princely states?
questions.explanation: The 26th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1971 formally abolished privy purses, privileges, and recognition of princely rulers under the Constitution of India.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement regarding the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act enacted in 1976 during the Emergency:
options: A) It restricted the tenure of the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from 5 years to 4 years.
B) It inserted the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' into the Preamble of the Constitution.
C) It incorporated Fundamental Duties for citizens under Article 51A.
D) It placed constitutional amendments beyond judicial scrutiny under Article 368.
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment did not reduce legislative tenure to 4 years; on the contrary, it extended the tenure of the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies from 5 years to 6 years.

questions.question: Under the terms of the historic Assam Accord signed in August 1985 between the Rajiv Gandhi government and the All Assam Students Union (AASU), what was the cut-off date agreed upon to identify and deport foreigners who entered Assam illegally?
questions.explanation: The Assam Accord stipulated that foreigners who entered Assam on or after 25 March 1971 were to be detected, deleted from electoral rolls, and deported.

questions.sub_topic: Baltic Independence and Collapse of USSR
questions.question: Which among the Soviet republics was the first to officially declare its independence from the USSR in March 1990, triggering the unraveling of the Soviet Union?
questions.explanation: Lithuania was the first Soviet republic to declare full restoration of its national independence on 11 March 1990, defying Moscow.

questions.sub_topic: Forms of Hegemony and Cultural Power
questions.question: Which of the following books authored by Susan Strange provides the classical analysis of US structural hegemony based on control over security, production, finance, and knowledge?
options: A) Bound to Lead: The Changing Nature of American Power (1990)
B) The Tragedy of Great Power Politics (2001)
C) Soft Power: The Means to Success in World Politics (2004)
questions.explanation: Susan Strange articulated the structural dimensions of global hegemony (security, production, credit/finance, and knowledge) in her seminal work 'States and Markets' (1988).

questions.question: In 1997, UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan initiated an inquiry into reforming the United Nations Security Council. Which of the following criteria was NOT recommended for inducting new permanent members?
options: A) Must possess confirmed nuclear weapons capability to maintain deterrence parity
B) A major economic power and a major contributor to the UN budget
C) A major military power and substantial contributor to UN peacekeeping
D) A nation that respects democracy and human rights and represents global cultural diversity
questions.explanation: Nuclear capability was never proposed as a criterion; rather, the criteria focused on population size, economic strength, budgetary contributions, commitment to human rights, and regional balance.

questions.question: The principle of 'Common But Differentiated Responsibilities' (CBDR) adopted at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit asserts that:
options: A) Every sovereign state must reduce greenhouse emissions by an identical percentage irrespective of economic size or past pollution.
B) Only developing countries must freeze industrial carbon emissions to preserve global atmospheric sinks.
C) All states share a collective responsibility to protect the global environment, but developed nations bear a heavier burden due to their historical emissions and greater technological capacity.
D) Developing nations are exempted from all environmental obligations and monitoring protocols forever.
questions.explanation: Principle 7 of the Rio Declaration states that while all countries share responsibility for environmental protection, developed countries acknowledge their special historical responsibility given their disproportionate contribution to global degradation and superior financial/technological resources.
